en: Up to date with the latest news or developments; side by side
hook: A-BREAST: chest to chest, side by side, keeping pace.
story: Abreast. Every morning before class, Tahmid reads two newspapers, scans the business headlines, and listens to a news podcast on the bus. When the economics professor asked about yesterday's change in interest rates, only Tahmid knew the answer. He keeps abreast of current events: up to date with the latest news and developments. Literally, abreast means side by side, like soldiers marching shoulder to shoulder. Keeping abreast of the news means marching level with it, never falling behind. Synonym: up to date.

gre.s: Researchers in such a fast-moving field must read constantly to stay ____ of new findings; otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months.
gre.clue: otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months

example: Farida reads three newspapers on her morning commute to keep abreast of the cricket board's latest selection decisions.

en: Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others
hook: ALTRUISTIC: ALTER (other) + TRUE care for others.
story: Altruistic. Every Friday, his only day off, Arif teaches street children at Kamalapur railway station to read. He buys the books with his own salary, brings biscuits, and has never once posted about it online. When a friend asked why he gave up his weekends, he said, "Somebody taught me once, for free." He is altruistic: showing selfless concern for others' well-being. Alter means other. Its opposite is selfish or egoistic.

gre.s: Although the donor claimed his motives were purely ____, critics noted that the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction.
gre.clue: the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction

example: Rahim's altruistic decision to donate a kidney to a stranger inspired dozens of people in his neighborhood to register as organ donors.

en: Without a clear shape, form, or structure
hook: A-MORPH-ous: 'a' means without, 'morph' means shape. Without shape.
story: Amorphous. Zayan's study plan began as a cloud of good intentions: "Study vocab sometime. Maybe math too." No days. No targets. No shape at all. A week later he had learned exactly nine words. His sister grabbed a marker and drew a grid on his wall: thirty words each morning, one quant set each night. The cloud became a staircase. Amorphous means having no clear shape or structure, like smoke you cannot hold. An amorphous plan is just a wish.

gre.s: The committee's proposal remained frustratingly ____: it gestured toward reform but specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency.
gre.clue: specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency

example: The protest movement remained amorphous for months, with no leaders, no headquarters, and no agreed list of demands.

en: Deviating from what is normal or expected
hook: A-NOMAL-ous: 'a-normal', not normal.
story: Anomalous. Nadia's GRE practice scores were steady: 310, 311, 309, 312. Then one Tuesday she scored 334. She screamed. She called her mother. Then her tutor looked closer and frowned. Nadia had accidentally taken a beginner-level practice test. The 334 was anomalous: it did not fit the pattern at all. Anomalous means deviating from what is normal or expected. In science passages, anomalous data are the strange results that challenge an accepted theory.

gre.s: Because every other sample showed the same chemical signature, researchers dismissed the one ____ reading as the result of contamination.
gre.clue: every other sample showed the same chemical signature

example: An anomalous spike in electricity use every midnight led auditors to discover an illegal cryptocurrency mining rig in the basement.

en: Something that is the exact reverse of another thing
hook: ANTI-THESIS: against the thesis, the exact opposite.
story: Antithesis. Twins Rafi and Rafa share a birthday and a bedroom, and nothing else. Rafi is loud, messy, and late for everything; his side of the room looks like a cyclone hit it. Rafa is quiet, organised, and arrives ten minutes early; her side looks like a museum. Their mother says Rafa is the antithesis of her brother: his exact opposite. Anti means against, thesis means a proposition. Cruelty is the antithesis of kindness.

gre.s: The minimalist new museum, with its bare white walls and empty spaces, is the ____ of the ornate palace that once stood on the site.
gre.clue: bare white walls and empty spaces

example: Shy and soft-spoken, the new captain was the antithesis of his loud predecessor, yet the players responded to him just as well.

en: The classic example of a type; the original pattern others copy
hook: ARCH-TYPE: the ARCH (chief, first) TYPE.
story: Archetype. Every Bengali child knows folk tales about the clever jackal who tricks the crocodile and the tiger. Hundreds of later stories follow the same pattern: a small, smart animal outwitting a bigger, stronger one. The clever jackal is an archetype: a very typical example, an original model from which others are copied. Arche means first or original, and type means model. Robin Hood is the archetype of the noble outlaw. Synonyms: prototype, model, paragon.

gre.s: The scheming stepmother of old folk tales is the ____ from which countless later villains, in novels and films alike, have been copied.
gre.clue: from which countless later villains

example: For many Bangladeshi readers, Himu has become the archetype of the carefree young man drifting through Dhaka in a yellow panjabi.

en: Showing bold willingness to take risks; daringly bold (sometimes rude)
hook: AUDACIOUS: 'AUDACity' — the nerve to do something bold.
story: Audacious. Two balls left. Twelve runs needed. The stadium was silent. The young batsman looked at the fastest bowler in the world, switched his hands mid-run-up, and reverse-swept the ball over the boundary for six. Then he did it again. The crowd exploded. It was risky, daring, almost reckless, and brilliant. Audacious means boldly willing to take risks. It can be admiring, like that shot, or critical: an audacious lie is told with shocking nerve.

gre.s: The startup's ____ plan to compete directly with three established giants struck investors as either visionary or reckless.
gre.clue: either visionary or reckless

example: In an audacious move, the chess prodigy sacrificed her queen in the opening, a gamble that stunned the grandmaster across the board.

en: To criticize someone strongly and officially; such official criticism
hook: CENSURE: like a CENSOR, it officially condemns what you did.
story: Censure. The minister had told parliament that the new bridge cost fifty crore taka. Then journalists found the real figure: one hundred and twenty crore. The parliament did not remove him from office, but it voted to censure him, a formal, public statement of strong disapproval written into the official record. His career never recovered. To censure is to criticize severely and officially. Do not confuse it with censor, which means to cut or ban content.

gre.s: The medical board voted to ____ the surgeon for his reckless conduct, though it stopped short of revoking his license.
gre.clue: his reckless conduct

example: Parliament censured the minister after an inquiry found he had hidden the true cost of the bridge from lawmakers.

en: Polite submission and respect for another's opinion or authority
hook: DEFERENCE: you DEFER, or step aside, out of respect.
story: Deference. In the village meeting, the young men argued loudly about where to build the new well. Then old Headman Abdul Karim raised one hand. Instantly, everyone fell silent. When he spoke, nobody interrupted, even those who disagreed with him. They lowered their eyes and listened. That is deference: polite, respectful submission to someone's judgment or authority. You defer, or step aside, out of respect. Out of deference to her parents, Sara delayed her trip.

gre.s: Out of ____ to the senior surgeon, the young resident kept her doubts to herself, a silence she later regretted.
gre.clue: kept her doubts to herself

example: In deference to her grandfather's wishes, Labiba held her wedding in the family's village home rather than a Dhaka convention hall.

en: Able to be noticed or understood, though perhaps with difficulty
bn: লক্ষণীয়; বোঝা বা দেখা যায় এমন
hook: DISCERN = to see clearly. DISCERNIBLE = can be seen.
story: Discernible. On the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway at dawn, the fog was so thick that Farhan could barely see the bonnet of his own car. The truck ahead was barely discernible: just two faint red lights glowing in the white haze. He slowed to a crawl and held his breath. Discernible means able to be seen, detected, or understood, though perhaps with difficulty. On the GRE, "no discernible difference" means the change is too small to detect.

gre.s: Although the forgery fooled most experts, a faint but ____ difference in the brushwork eventually gave it away.
gre.clue: eventually gave it away

example: By the third week of the new diet, there was a discernible improvement in his blood pressure, though he still felt tired.

en: Causing one to feel unsettled or uneasy
hook: DIS-CONCERT-ING: throws the CONCERT out of tune.
story: Disconcerting. During her visa interview, Ishita answered every question carefully. The officer said nothing. He simply stared at her file and kept writing for two full minutes without looking up. The silence was disconcerting: it made her feel unsettled and uneasy. A painting whose eyes seem to follow you around the room is disconcerting too. Concert suggests harmony, and dis breaks it: something disconcerting throws you out of tune. Synonyms: unsettling, unnerving, disquieting.

gre.s: Audiences found the film's abrupt shifts in tone ____: scenes of broad slapstick gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality.
gre.clue: gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality

example: It was disconcerting to hear my own voice played back on the radio, slightly higher and faster than I had imagined it.

en: Not sincere; pretending to know less than one does
hook: DIS-INGENUOUS: NOT ingenuous (innocent). Fake innocence.
story: Disingenuous. The exam questions had been leaked, and one student had shared them in three WhatsApp groups. When the principal asked him about it, he widened his eyes. "Leaked? Me? I had no idea the questions were leaked, sir!" Everyone knew he had shared them. His surprise was disingenuous: insincere, pretending to know less than he did. Dis means not, ingenuous means innocent. Disingenuous means fake innocence. Its opposite is candid.

gre.s: It is ____ of the company to claim it was unaware of the defect, since internal emails show executives discussed it for months.
gre.clue: internal emails show executives discussed it for months

example: Calling the fee hike a 'small adjustment' was disingenuous, since tuition at the private university rose by nearly forty percent.

en: To tell something that was meant to stay private
hook: DIVULGE: DIVE into the secrets and BULGE them out.
story: Divulge. Arif's best friend told him a secret: she was applying to Oxford, but she did not want anyone to know in case she was rejected. Arif promised not to tell. Two days later, at a family dinner, he accidentally mentioned it. Her mother called within the hour. He had divulged her secret: revealed private or sensitive information. Doctors cannot divulge patient information. Synonyms: disclose, reveal.

gre.s: The journalist went to prison rather than ____ the identity of her source.
gre.clue: went to prison rather than

example: Even after ten years, my aunt refuses to divulge the secret ingredient that makes her mutton curry so famous at family weddings.

en: Refusing to give up, even when progress is slow or hard
hook: DOGGED: like a DOG holding a bone, refusing to let go.
story: Dogged. Mitu failed the GRE twice. After the second result, she cried for one evening. The next morning she woke at five, opened her notebook, and began again. Every day for six more months: vocabulary at dawn, quant at night, a full test every Saturday. On her third attempt she scored 326. She had shown dogged determination: stubborn, persistent, refusing to quit. Think of a dog with a bone. A dogged detective never drops a case.

gre.s: Thanks to her ____ persistence, the reporter eventually uncovered the scandal that others had abandoned after a few weeks.
gre.clue: that others had abandoned after a few weeks

example: Through dogged practice every dawn on the Rajshahi riverbank, the young sprinter shaved a full second off her best time.

en: Ecstatically happy
hook: ELATED: ELEVATED with joy.
story: Elated. At midnight, Nadia's phone buzzed with an email from Germany. She opened it, read the first line, read it again, and screamed. Full scholarship. She ran into her parents' room, jumped on the bed, hugged her mother, called her grandmother, and danced in the kitchen until two in the morning. She was elated: ecstatically happy and excited. Think: elevated with joy, floating above the ground. It is the opposite of crestfallen.

gre.s: The team was ____ after the unexpected victory, celebrating late into the night in the streets of their small town.
gre.clue: celebrating late into the night

example: The astronomers were elated when the telescope finally captured a clear image of the comet they had tracked for six years.

en: Able to understand and share the feelings of others
hook: EMPATHETIC: feeling IN (em) someone else's pain (pathos).
story: Empathetic. When Sara failed her driving test, most friends said, "Never mind, try again." But Ishita sat beside her and said, "I remember how humiliated I felt when I failed mine. It is awful." For the first time that day, Sara felt understood. Ishita was empathetic: able to understand and share the feelings of others. Sympathy is feeling sorry for someone; empathy is feeling with them, as if in their place. Synonyms: understanding, compassionate, sensitive.

gre.s: The best nurses are not only technically skilled but also ____, able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety and respond to it before a word is spoken.
gre.clue: able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety

example: An empathetic coach, Sharmin noticed whenever a player was struggling at home and quietly lightened her training load.

en: Making great demands on skill, attention, or effort
bn: কঠোর পরিশ্রম দাবি করে এমন; অতি খুঁতখুঁতে
hook: EXACTING: demands everything to be EXACT.
story: Exacting. Ishita's violin teacher accepted nothing less than perfection. Every note had to be exactly in tune. Every finger had to fall in exactly the right place. One tiny mistake, and the whole piece began again from the first bar. Lessons sometimes lasted three hours. The teacher was exacting: making great demands on skill, attention, and effort. Think: everything must be exact. An exacting task stretches you to your limit.

gre.s: The surgeon's ____ standards, which allowed no margin for error, made her residency program one of the most demanding in the country.
gre.clue: which allowed no margin for error

example: Restoring the old Armenian church in Dhaka was exacting work, as each cracked tile had to be matched by hand to the original.

en: Intensely irritated and frustrated
hook: EXASPERATED: EX-ASP, bitten by a snake of annoyance.
story: Exasperated. Mitu explained the math problem to her little brother once. He nodded. She asked him to solve it. He could not. She explained again, slower. Again. With drawings. With apples. After the fifth time, when he asked, "Wait, what is a fraction?", she threw her hands in the air. She was exasperated: intensely irritated and frustrated, especially after repeated problems. Exasperation is the feeling of reaching the end of your patience.

gre.s: After the airline cancelled his flight for the third time in a week, the ____ traveler finally gave up and rented a car.
gre.clue: for the third time in a week

example: Exasperated by the endless traffic jams on Mirpur Road, Kamal finally bought a bicycle and began riding to his office.

en: Imaginative but unrealistic
hook: FANCY-full: full of fancy imagination.
story: Fanciful. As a little girl, Joya believed her grandmother's stories about fairies living in the old banyan tree. She drew pictures of tiny castles among its roots and left rice for the fairies every evening. Now she is twenty-two, but she still loves fanciful ideas: flying cars, cities on Mars, talking robots. Fanciful means imaginative but unrealistic. A fanciful explanation is creative and charming, but unlikely to be true. Think: full of fancy.

gre.s: The historian dismissed the legend as ____, pointing out that no record from the period mentions a sea monster at all.
gre.clue: no record from the period mentions

example: Most engineers thought his scheme of floating solar farms on every village pond was fanciful, until a pilot project actually worked.

en: Unnecessary and unjustified; given free of charge
hook: GRATUITOUS: like a GRATUITY (tip), extra and not required.
story: Gratuitous. A new action film had a simple, touching love story, but the director added a ten minute scene of bloody violence that had nothing to do with the plot. Critics called the scene gratuitous: unnecessary and unjustified, added only to shock. Gratuitous shares a root with gratis, meaning free, so it can also mean given free of charge. On the GRE, though, it usually means uncalled for, as in a gratuitous insult. Synonyms: needless, unwarranted, unprovoked.

gre.s: The reviewer's remarks about the author's appearance were entirely ____: they had no bearing on the quality of the novel and served only to humiliate her.
gre.clue: had no bearing on the quality of the novel

example: The coach's gratuitous insults after the defeat hurt the young players far more than the scoreline itself.

en: Peculiar to an individual; distinctive and unusual
hook: IDIO-SYNCRATIC: IDIO means one's own (as in idiom).
story: Idiosyncratic. Professor Haque always lectures barefoot, writes on the board only with his left hand, and opens every class by singing a line from Lalon. His students imitate him affectionately. His habits are idiosyncratic: peculiar to him alone, distinctive and unusual. Idios is Greek for one's own, the same root as idiom. An idiosyncrasy is one such personal quirk. An idiosyncratic writing style is instantly recognisable as one person's. Synonyms: quirky, eccentric, peculiar.

gre.s: The novelist's spelling and punctuation are so ____ that editors hesitate to correct them, fearing they would erase the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable.
gre.clue: the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable

example: The professor's idiosyncratic grading system awarded extra marks for the questions students asked rather than the answers they gave.

en: Dull and tedious because of lack of variety
hook: MONO-TONE: one tone, over and over.
story: Monotonous. At the factory, Kamal's job was to put the same bolt into the same hole on the same machine part. Eight thousand times a day. Six days a week. Same sound, same motion, same view. After a month, he felt his mind switching off by ten in the morning. His work was monotonous: dull and tedious because nothing ever changed. Mono means one, tone means sound: one single note, forever.

gre.s: The ____ landscape, mile after mile of identical wheat fields, made the long drive feel endless.
gre.clue: mile after mile of identical wheat fields

example: The lecturer's monotonous voice, never rising or falling, sent half the back row to sleep before the tea break.

en: To force someone out of a position or place
hook: OUST: kick OUT.
story: Oust. For five straight years, the company lost money. Products failed. Staff quit. Investors grew furious. Finally, at a tense board meeting, the directors voted to remove the CEO, and security escorted him out of the building that same afternoon. He had been ousted: forced out of his position against his will. Think: kicked out. Popular movements have ousted many rulers throughout history; shareholders can oust a failing executive.

gre.s: The rebels' attempt to ____ the dictator failed when the army remained loyal to him.
gre.clue: when the army remained loyal to him

example: Shareholders voted to oust the chief executive after the company lost a third of its value in a single year.

en: To tell someone you are disappointed by what they did; such criticism
hook: REPROACH: re-APPROACH someone to tell them they disappointed you.
story: Reproach. Tanvir forgot his mother's birthday. Completely. That evening, she did not shout. She simply looked at him with sad, quiet eyes and said, "I waited all evening for your call." Then she went back to cooking. That single look hurt more than any scolding. To reproach is to express disappointment or disapproval to someone. A look of reproach can be devastating. Beyond reproach means so perfect that nobody can criticize you.

gre.s: Rather than ____ the young employee for his mistake, the manager calmly showed him how to avoid it in the future.
gre.clue: calmly showed him how to avoid it in the future

example: My mother never shouted, but she could reproach us with a single look whenever we forgot to greet guests at the door.

en: Severely critical; harsh
hook: SCATHING: leaves you SCARRED and burned.
story: Scathing. The director spent four years and fifty crore taka on his new film. On the opening night, the country's most feared critic published her review: "Two hours and forty minutes of my life that I will never get back. The acting is wooden, the plot is absurd, and the songs are crimes." The director did not sleep that night. Her review was scathing: severely critical and harsh. Unscathed means unharmed.

gre.s: The auditor's ____ report, which described the agency's management as reckless and incompetent, led to the director's immediate resignation.
gre.clue: described the agency's management as reckless and incompetent

example: The opposition leader gave a scathing speech in parliament, accusing the government of ignoring families displaced by the floods.

en: Not genuine; false or fake
hook: SPURIOUS: SPURred by lies, false.
story: Spurious. The job applicant's certificate looked perfect: an official stamp, a signature, a university logo. But when the company emailed the university, the reply came back in an hour: no such student had ever graduated. The certificate was spurious: fake, not genuine. Spurious also describes false reasoning or faulty data. Spurious and specious are cousins: specious looks right but is wrong, while spurious is simply counterfeit.

gre.s: Scholars have shown that the letter, long attributed to the queen, is ____, a forgery produced nearly a century after her death.
gre.clue: a forgery produced nearly a century after her death

example: The supplement company's spurious claim that its pills cured diabetes led the health ministry to ban the product.

en: To weaken or overturn an established system or authority, often secretly
hook: SUB-VERT: turn (vert) from below (sub), flipping the system upside down.
story: Subvert. The rebels did not attack the government head-on. Instead, they worked from inside: spreading rumours, bribing officials, and slowly turning soldiers against their commanders. Within a year, the regime collapsed without a single battle. They had subverted it: undermined an established authority or system from within. Sub means under, vert means turn. Artists can subvert expectations too, by breaking the usual rules of a genre.

gre.s: The director's films ____ the conventions of the horror genre, revealing the monster in the first scene and making the audience sympathize with it.
gre.clue: revealing the monster in the first scene

example: Election observers accused local officials of trying to subvert the vote by moving polling stations at the last minute.

en: Accepted or suggested silently, without being put into words
hook: TACIT: TACITURN, silent agreement.
story: Tacit. Mahin and his roommate share one small desk. Nobody ever discussed it, but Mahin uses it from seven to nine every evening, and his roommate takes over afterwards. They never quarrel about it. Their arrangement is tacit: understood without being stated. Tacit comes from the Latin for silent, the same root as taciturn, meaning a person of few words. Silence can signal tacit approval: by saying nothing, you agree. Synonyms: implicit, unspoken.

gre.s: Although the treaty never explicitly mentioned the disputed island, both nations had reached a ____ understanding that neither would station troops there.
gre.clue: never explicitly mentioned

example: By tacit agreement, the two brothers never mentioned their late father's debts at the dinner table.

en: To emphasize or draw attention to
hook: UNDERSCORE: draw a line UNDER a word to highlight it.
story: Underscore. The doctor sat down beside Imran's grandmother. "Listen carefully," she said. "Rest. Not when you feel like it. Rest every single day for two weeks. No cooking, no climbing stairs, no exceptions." She repeated it twice more, tapping the table each time. Nobody could miss the point. She had underscored it: emphasized and drawn attention to it, like drawing a line under important words. The rising toll underscored the need for safer roads.

gre.s: Bridge collapses like last week's ____ the urgent need for the repairs that engineers have requested for years.
gre.clue: that engineers have requested for years

example: The record heat waves of recent summers underscore how urgently Dhaka needs more trees and shaded public spaces.

en: Truthfulness; accuracy
hook: VERACITY: VERy accurate. 'Vera' means true.
story: Veracity. In a speech, the minister claimed that unemployment had fallen by half in a single year. Journalists checked every source: government data, surveys, international reports. Nothing supported the claim. Newspapers questioned the veracity of his statement: its truthfulness and accuracy. Vera means true. Do not confuse veracity with voracity, which means a huge appetite. A witness whose veracity is doubted will not be believed.

gre.s: Historians question the ____ of the memoir, noting that several events it describes could not possibly have happened.
gre.clue: could not possibly have happened

example: Before publishing the leaked photographs, the editors spent two days checking their veracity with independent forensic experts.
